stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.15.2, using keyboard and mouse in a new single-player Creative-mode world. The Creative inventory GUI must remain open during the trigger. The report does not require a particular seed, coordinates, commands, dedicated server, or additional players.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start exactly Java Edition 1.15.2, the first version listed as affected. Do not use fix version 24w33a for this reproduction.
Ensure the Inventory control is bound to E and the Drop Selected Item control is bound to Q, matching the report's inputs. If controls have been rebound, restore these bindings before beginning.
Use the single-item trigger variant selected for this plan: press Q without Ctrl while hovering over a hotbar stack containing exactly one item.
A new Creative world is used as a practical way to begin with an empty hotbar; no particular world seed or world type is required.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the Java Edition installation or profile for version 1.15.2 and start the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft Java Edition main menu is displayed and identifies the running version as 1.15.2.

steps.action: From the main menu, open the single-player world list.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Begin creating a fresh world so the test starts with an empty inventory and hotbar.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set the new world's game mode to Creative. Click the Game Mode button until its displayed value is Creative; the world name, seed, and other settings may remain at their defaults.
steps.exact_input: Click Game Mode until it reads Game Mode: Creative
steps.success_cue: The world creation screen displays Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Create and enter the world.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the world and can move normally.

steps.action: Wait until initial terrain loading is complete before opening the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, the loading overlay is gone, and player movement responds normally.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory GUI is open, showing category tabs, an item grid, and the nine hotbar slots along the bottom.

steps.action: Select a Creative category other than Survival Inventory and Search Items. For this deterministic path, select the Combat tab, identifiable by its sword icon. Do not select the Search Items tab because keyboard input there can be captured by the search field.
steps.success_cue: The Combat tab is selected and its weapons and armor are visible in the item grid; neither Search Items nor Survival Inventory is selected.

steps.action: Locate a Diamond Sword in the Combat tab's item grid, using the tooltip shown when hovering if necessary, and pick it up with the cursor. A Diamond Sword is used because it is non-stackable, ensuring the test stack contains exactly one item.
steps.success_cue: A single Diamond Sword icon is attached to the mouse cursor.

steps.action: Place the cursor-held Diamond Sword into any empty slot in the hotbar, which is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the Creative inventory GUI.
steps.success_cue: The selected hotbar slot contains exactly one Diamond Sword, the mouse cursor is no longer holding an item, and the Combat tab remains open.

steps.action: Move the mouse pointer over the hotbar slot containing the Diamond Sword without clicking or closing the inventory.
steps.exact_input: Move pointer over the Diamond Sword hotbar slot
steps.success_cue: The Diamond Sword's hotbar slot is highlighted under the pointer while the Combat tab remains selected.

steps.action: With the pointer still hovering over the one-item Diamond Sword stack, press the Drop Selected Item key once. Do not hold Left Ctrl for this single-item variant, and do not close the inventory before pressing the key.
steps.success_cue: The Q input has been issued while a one-item hotbar stack was hovered and a Creative tab other than Search Items or Survival Inventory remained open.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just pressed Q once while hovering over the one-item Diamond Sword stack in the hotbar, with the Creative inventory still open on the Combat tab. Begin observation immediately without performing another inventory action.
uncertainties: The report provides two alternative triggers: Q for a one-item stack and Ctrl+Q for a multi-item stack. This plan selects the one-item Q variant because it is the simplest deterministic reproduction; the Ctrl+Q variant is not separately executed.
The specific Combat tab and Diamond Sword are practical choices. The report permits any Creative tab other than Survival Inventory and Search Items and states that the issue works with any item.
A new single-player world is used for operational simplicity. The report specifies Creative mode but does not require a particular world, server type, seed, or location.

source_meta._title: Frogspawn is not grouped with turtle eggs in the Creative inventory

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 22w12a, running as a client with keyboard-and-mouse UI. Use a newly created single-player world in Creative mode as the simplest execution context; the report does not require a particular seed, coordinates, server, command permissions, datapack, or multiplayer configuration.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is installed and can launch the historical Java Edition snapshot 22w12a.
Use snapshot 22w12a, the first version listed as affected. Do not use fix version 22w42a for this reproduction.
The executor can create a new single-player world. No existing world data is required.
If controls have been rebound, use the key assigned to the Inventory action instead of the default E key.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select a Java Edition installation configured to use the exact version snapshot 22w12a.
steps.success_cue: The selected launcher installation lists its Minecraft version as 22w12a.

steps.action: Launch the selected 22w12a installation and wait for the Minecraft title screen to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is responsive and the displayed version information identifies the running game as 22w12a.

steps.action: Select the Singleplayer button on the main menu.
steps.success_cue: The Select World screen is open.

steps.action: Select Create New World. An existing world is unnecessary because this reproduction only requires access to the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen is open and displays the game-mode setting.

steps.action: Select the game-mode control until it reads Game Mode: Creative. Leave the world seed and other settings at their defaults because the report specifies none.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen explicitly shows that Creative mode is selected.

steps.action: Select Create New World to generate the world, then wait until terrain has rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the loaded world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Open the player inventory by pressing the key assigned to the Inventory action; the default keyboard key is E.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is visible with category tabs and a grid of items, rather than the Survival crafting-only inventory.

steps.action: Move the pointer over the Creative inventory category tabs one at a time until the tab tooltip or label reads Miscellaneous. Do not use the Search Items tab, because the report specifically tests ordering within the Miscellaneous category.
steps.success_cue: The pointer is over the category tab identified as Miscellaneous.

steps.action: Left-click the Miscellaneous category tab once.
steps.success_cue: The Miscellaneous tab is selected and its item grid is displayed.

steps.action: Prepare the category for a complete top-to-bottom inspection by moving its scrollbar to the top. With the pointer over the item grid, scroll upward until no further upward movement occurs, or drag the scrollbar thumb to its highest position if necessary.
steps.success_cue: The Miscellaneous tab remains selected and its scrollbar is at the top of the category contents.

stor.handoff_condition: Snapshot 22w12a is running in a Creative-mode world, the Creative inventory is open, the Miscellaneous category is selected, and its contents are positioned at the top. Begin inspecting the category's item ordering for the Turtle Egg and Frogspawn entries without changing to the Search Items tab.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player or multiplayer. Single-player is selected as the simplest practical context because the reported reproduction concerns the client-side Creative inventory and lists no server requirement.

The report only says to look through the Miscellaneous tab and does not specify an initial scroll position. Resetting the category to the top is an execution aid for deterministic inspection and is not claimed as a report requirement.
Current Minecraft Launcher navigation may differ by launcher build, but the game version selected for reproduction must remain exactly 22w12a.

source_meta._title: Muddy mangrove roots are not grouped with mud in the Creative inventory

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 22w14a in a single-player Creative-mode world. No particular world seed, coordinates, dimension, difficulty, commands, server, or additional players are required.
preconditions: Configure the Minecraft Launcher to start Java Edition version 22w14a, the first version listed as affected in the report.
Use the Creative inventory as it appears in 22w14a; do not use the fixed version 22w42a, whose inventory categories and ordering differ.
Create or load a world in Creative mode so the category-based Creative inventory is available.
Use the Building Blocks tab itself when locating the items. Do not substitute the Search Items tab, because the category ordering under test must remain visible.
If controls have been rebound, use the control assigned to Open/Close Inventory instead of the default E key.

steps.action: Start Minecraft Java Edition using a launcher installation configured for snapshot 22w14a. Wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is displayed and the on-screen version text identifies the running version as 22w14a.

steps.action: Create a single-player world in Creative mode. From the main menu, select Singleplayer, select Create New World, change the game mode until it reads Creative, and then create the world. No specific seed or other world option is needed.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The world has loaded, terrain is rendered, normal input responds, and the player is in Creative mode.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Open/Close Inventory control. The default keyboard input is E.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory window is open and category tabs are visible around the item grid.

steps.action: Select the Building Blocks category. Move the pointer across the category tabs until the tooltip reads Building Blocks, then left-click that tab. In this inventory layout, the tab can also be recognized by its building-block icon.
steps.exact_input: Left-click the tab whose tooltip reads "Building Blocks"
steps.success_cue: The Building Blocks tab is selected and its category-specific item grid and vertical scroll control are visible.

steps.action: Locate Dirt within the Building Blocks tab. Browse only this tab by rotating the mouse wheel while the pointer is over the item grid, or by dragging the vertical scrollbar. Hover candidate items without clicking them until a tooltip reading Dirt appears. Note its position in the category sequence so it can later be compared with the other named items.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or vertical scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Dirt"
steps.success_cue: An item in the Building Blocks grid has been unambiguously identified by the tooltip Dirt.

steps.action: Locate Rooted Dirt in the same Building Blocks category. Continue browsing the category grid and hover candidate items until the tooltip reads Rooted Dirt. Note its position relative to the previously located Dirt item. Do not switch to the Search Items tab.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or vertical scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Rooted Dirt"
steps.success_cue: An item in the Building Blocks grid has been unambiguously identified by the tooltip Rooted Dirt, with the earlier Dirt position retained for comparison.

steps.action: Locate Mud in the same Building Blocks category. Continue browsing with the mouse wheel or scrollbar and hover candidate items until the tooltip reads Mud. Note its position in the category sequence.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or vertical scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Mud"
steps.success_cue: An item in the Building Blocks grid has been unambiguously identified by the tooltip Mud.

steps.action: Locate Muddy Mangrove Roots in the same Building Blocks category. Continue browsing the category grid and hover candidate items until the tooltip reads Muddy Mangrove Roots. Keep the Creative inventory open after identifying it, with the prior locations of Dirt, Rooted Dirt, and Mud retained for comparison.
steps.exact_input: Mouse wheel or vertical scrollbar; hover until tooltip reads "Muddy Mangrove Roots"
steps.success_cue: The Muddy Mangrove Roots item has been identified by its tooltip while the Building Blocks category remains selected.

stor.handoff_condition: The Creative inventory is still open on the Building Blocks tab in Java Edition 22w14a, and Dirt, Rooted Dirt, Mud, and Muddy Mangrove Roots have all been located in that category sequence. Hand off now for inspection of their relative inventory placement.
uncertainties: The report does not provide a world seed, coordinates, GUI scale, language setting, or resource-pack configuration; none appears necessary to reach the inventory ordering under test.
The exact row and scroll position of each item are intentionally not supplied because those positions constitute what the separate observation subsystem must inspect.

Creating a new single-player Creative world is a practical execution choice; the report only requires access to the Creative inventory and does not state that a new world or single-player mode is mandatory.

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 23w44a in a single-player world with the Update 1.21 experiment and commands enabled. Creative mode is used as a practical setup choice so a Crafting Table can be obtained without unrelated gathering or crafting.
preconditions: Install or select the exact Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 23w44a in the Minecraft Launcher; snapshots may need to be enabled on the Launcher's Installations tab.
Use a disposable test world or a separate game directory because snapshots can damage worlds.
Use the standard in-game crafting-table recipe book; do not install a data pack that adds, removes, or changes recipes.
If the game is not using English, identify controls by their equivalent localized labels; the exact search input remains "waxed".

steps.action: Start Minecraft: Java Edition using the 23w44a launcher installation. At the title screen, check the version text in the lower-left corner before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is open and its version text identifies the running version as 23w44a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to open the world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen is visible.

steps.action: On the Game settings, set Game Mode to Creative. Creative mode is not stated as a requirement by the report; it is selected only to obtain and place the Crafting Table deterministically.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Set Allow Commands to ON so the report's recipe-unlocking command can be executed after entering the world.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows that commands are allowed.

steps.action: Open the Experiments menu on the world-creation screen, enable the experiment named Update 1.21, and return to the main world-creation screen. Accept the experimental-world confirmation if one is displayed.
steps.success_cue: Update 1.21 is enabled for the world being created, and the world-creation screen indicates that experiments are active.

steps.action: Select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: World generation begins.

steps.action: Wait until the world finishes loading. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible; wait until terrain has rendered and normal player movement responds.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in the generated world, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Press T, the default Open Chat control, to open the in-game chat input.
steps.success_cue: The chat input line is open and ready to receive a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's recipe command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a syntax or permission error, and command feedback indicates that recipes were granted to the current player.

steps.action: Press E, the default Inventory control, to open the Creative inventory. Select the Search Items tab, represented by a compass icon, if that tab is not already active.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open with its item-search field available.

steps.action: Click the Creative inventory search field and enter the item name.
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table item appears among the filtered Creative inventory results.

steps.action: Move one Crafting Table item from the search results into the far-left hotbar slot at the bottom of the inventory, then press E or Escape to close the inventory. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots used while playing.
steps.success_cue: The inventory is closed and a Crafting Table icon is present in the first, far-left hotbar slot.

steps.action: Press 1, the default key for selecting the first hotbar slot, so the Crafting Table becomes the active held item.
steps.success_cue: The first hotbar slot is highlighted and the player is visibly holding a Crafting Table.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the top of a nearby solid ground block with empty space above it, then right-click once to place the Crafting Table.
steps.success_cue: A Crafting Table block is placed within interaction range of the player.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the placed Crafting Table and right-click it once to open its crafting interface.
steps.success_cue: The Crafting Table interface is open and shows a 3-by-3 crafting grid.

steps.action: If the recipe-book panel is not visible beside the crafting grid, click the recipe-book toggle button, represented by a green book, once. If the panel is already visible, leave it open.
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book panel is visible and includes a recipe search field.

steps.action: Ensure the recipe book is displaying all unlocked recipes rather than only recipes currently craftable from carried ingredients. If the filter is set to Showing Craftable, click its toggle so its tooltip/state becomes Showing All.
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book filter is set to Showing All.

steps.action: Click inside the recipe-book search field. If it contains existing text, select and delete that text so the field is empty.
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book search field is focused and contains no text.

steps.action: Type the report's search term into the focused recipe-book search field. Do not click any result after entering the term; immediately hand control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The recipe-book search field contains "waxed" and matching waxed-item recipe icons are displayed in the results area.

stor.handoff_condition: The Crafting Table interface and its recipe book are open, the filter is set to Showing All, and the search field has just been populated with "waxed" so the matching recipe results are visible. Begin inspecting the recipe-result entries and their grouping without performing another player action.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only as a deterministic way to obtain the Crafting Table and is not asserted to be required for the bug.

The report permits optionally appending " c", " e", " w", or " o" to isolate regular, exposed, weathered, or oxidized entries. This plan uses the base search "waxed" because it is the report's primary reproduction path and exposes all matching variants at once.

The experiment-selection menu wording or placement may differ slightly with language, window size, or GUI scale, but the experiment enabled for the recommended version must be the one named Update 1.21.

Later comments narrow which block types remain affected in later game versions. This plan intentionally follows the original reproduction in 23w44a because 23w44a is the first version in the report's affected-version list.
The report does not state whether third-party recipe-altering data packs were present. Avoiding them is an interference-control measure rather than a reported prerequisite.

stor.environment: Unmodified Minecraft Java Edition 1.8 running on two separate clients with two distinct authenticated player accounts. Use the viewer's client to host a LAN world with commands enabled. The viewer must remain in Creative mode or another non-Spectator mode; the target player will be changed to Spectator mode. The target account must use a skin whose head has a clearly visible, high-contrast outer/hat layer. Do not use client mods or resource packs that replace the player list, player models, or skins.
preconditions: Two distinct authenticated Minecraft Java Edition accounts are available and can be logged in simultaneously on separate clients.
Both clients can run the exact recommended version, Minecraft 1.8, and can connect through LAN or an equivalent local multiplayer setup.

The target account has an equipped custom skin containing opaque, visually distinctive pixels in the head's secondary/hat layer; for example, contrasting hair, glasses, a hood, or a mask extending beyond the base face.
The target client's Skin Customization setting for Hat is enabled.
The viewer can host the world with cheats/commands enabled and execute a game-mode command targeting the other player's exact username.
The default List Players control is Tab; if controls were rebound, use the key assigned to List Players instead.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher on both machines or client instances, create or select an installation using the exact release version Minecraft 1.8. Do not select 1.8.1, a later release, or the fix version.
steps.success_cue: Both launcher installations display Minecraft 1.8 as the selected version.

steps.action: Ensure the target account has a custom skin whose head outer/hat layer is easy to distinguish from its base face. If necessary, configure the skin through the Minecraft Launcher's Java Edition skin controls by uploading and selecting an appropriate PNG skin. Minecraft's official skin instructions confirm that a Java skin can be uploaded and selected through the launcher. ([help.minecraft.net](https://help.minecraft.net/hc/es-es/articles/4408894664461-Como-criar-uma-skin-personalizada-no-Minecraft-Java-Edition?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: A valid Java Edition skin PNG with a clearly contrasting head outer/hat layer
steps.success_cue: The target account's selected skin visibly includes distinctive pixels in the secondary layer surrounding the head or face.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft 1.8 on both clients, signing the viewer and target clients into different accounts. Wait for each client to reach the Minecraft main menu.
steps.success_cue: Both clients are at the Minecraft 1.8 main menu and display different authenticated usernames.

steps.action: On the target client, open Options, then Skin Customization, and click the Hat setting until it reads ON. Return to the main menu after changing it.
steps.success_cue: The target client's Skin Customization screen shows Hat: ON.

steps.action: On the viewer client, create a simple command-enabled Creative world: select Singleplayer, select Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, open More World Options, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and create the world. Remain near the initial spawn position after terrain loads.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> More World Options... -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The viewer is standing in a loaded Minecraft 1.8 world in Creative mode and can move normally.

steps.action: On the viewer client, press Esc, select Open to LAN, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and select Start LAN World. Note the confirmation message and port if Minecraft displays one.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Open to LAN -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Start LAN World
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the local game has been hosted, making the world available to another client.

steps.action: On the target client, select Multiplayer, wait for the LAN world to appear, select it, and choose Join Server. If LAN discovery is unavailable, connect through the equivalent direct LAN address without changing the two-player multiplayer condition.
steps.exact_input: Multiplayer -> detected LAN world -> Join Server
steps.success_cue: The target client enters the same world as the viewer and surrounding terrain finishes rendering.

steps.action: On the viewer client, briefly press and release the List Players control, which is Tab by default, to verify both players are connected. Do not evaluate the target icon's skin layers during this connectivity check.
steps.success_cue: The player-list overlay opens and contains entries for both the viewer username and the target username; the overlay then closes when Tab is released.

steps.action: Bring the two players close enough that the viewer can see the target's full player model. If they did not join near each other, press F3 on both clients to display coordinates, then use W, A, S, and D on the target client until the target's X and Z coordinates are within approximately 8 blocks of the viewer's X and Z coordinates. Close the debug screen with F3 afterward.
steps.success_cue: The target player's body and head are rendered directly in the viewer's world view at close range.

steps.action: From the viewer client, look directly at the target player's head and confirm that the selected skin has a visible outer/hat layer in the in-world model. If the target appears as a default skin or the head has no discernible outer layer, stop and correct the target's skin or Hat setting before continuing.
steps.success_cue: A clearly contrasting outer layer is visible around part of the target's head or face in the normal in-world player model.

steps.action: Keep the viewer in Creative mode and do not place the viewer in Spectator mode. The viewer may verify Creative mode by confirming that the Creative hotbar is present and that double-tapping Space enables flight.
steps.exact_input: Space, Space (only if a mode check is needed)
steps.success_cue: The viewer remains in a non-Spectator game mode while the target is still connected.

steps.action: On the viewer/host client, press T to open the in-game chat and command entry field.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open on the viewer client and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Replace TARGET_USERNAME with the target player's exact connected username, type the command with the leading slash, and press Enter. The numeric game-mode value 3 is the version-compatible Spectator value for Java Edition 1.8. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Minecraft_in_education/Minecraft_Vocabulary?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The host receives command feedback indicating that the target player's game mode was changed, with no unknown-command, permission, or player-not-found error.

steps.action: On the target client, wait for the game-mode change to finish. Confirm Spectator mode by checking that the normal survival/creative hotbar is replaced by the Spectator interface and that the target can fly through solid blocks. Do not disconnect or leave the world. Spectator mode in Java Edition permits flight and passage through blocks. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AProjects/Indonesian_translation/Mode_Penonton?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: W and Space while moving toward/through a solid block, if a mode check is needed
steps.success_cue: The target is in Spectator mode and remains connected, while the viewer remains non-Spectator.

steps.action: On the viewer client, press and continue holding the List Players control, which is Tab by default. Keep the key held so the multiplayer player-list overlay remains visible, then immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without changing either player's game mode or connection state.
steps.success_cue: The player-list overlay is open on the viewer client and contains the connected target player's entry while the target is in Spectator mode.

stor.handoff_condition: The non-Spectator viewer is holding the List Players control with the player-list overlay open, both usernames are present, and the target player is currently connected in Spectator mode with a confirmed skin containing a distinctive head outer/hat layer. Begin observing the target player's head icon without releasing Tab or changing either player's state.
uncertainties: The report permits either a multiplayer server or a LAN server and permits either a Spectator-mode target or a distant/unrendered target. This plan selects the LAN plus Spectator-mode route because it is the shortest deterministic branch supported by the report.

The report does not supply a skin file or target account. A suitable custom skin must therefore be selected as a practical setup choice; it must contain a visually obvious head outer/hat layer so the relevant rendering state can be distinguished.
The target player's username is not supplied. TARGET_USERNAME in the command must be replaced with the exact username shown in the connected player list.
The report does not specify which player hosts the LAN world. This plan makes the viewer the host so that the viewer can reliably execute the game-mode command while remaining non-Spectator.

The historical Skin Customization menu path was not independently verified from an accessible version-specific page. If the wording differs slightly in the installed 1.8 client, locate the skin-parts customization screen and enable the setting named Hat.
